## Captain's intent
Create the foundation for visual-first HTML notes for Active Physics Book 5 Chapter 1, which is syllabus chapter 25 Radiation and Radioactivity.

Project goal: HTML notes that prioritize interactive or non-interactive visual diagrams, minimize text, follow textbook order, and include concept checks. Sources are Active Physics textbooks, classified HKDSE papers, and the Book 5 Ch.1 question bank.

This task is only the first substep plus the project rule:
1. Consume and understand Book 5 Chapter 1 materials (OCR transcript, extract reusable images, shortlist relevant HKDSE and QB problems in textbook order).
2. Then add a Cursor project rule scoped to `notes/**` that captures these notes needs so later note-writing sessions follow them.

Do not write the full HTML chapter notes yet.

## Firstmate spec
Mode is local-only. Deliver committed artifacts on branch `fm/p2n-b5ch1-book-5-ch1-radiation-notes-intake-ocr-im-0b` only; no push, no PR.

### Source paths (read-only; untracked in git)
The disposable worktree will not contain these directories. Read them from the primary project path without modifying them:
- Textbook: `/Users/sinchunyeung/github/paper2notes/active-physics/Book 5.pdf` (112 pages; Chapter 1 = Radiation and Radioactivity / Ch.25)
- HKDSE bank: `/Users/sinchunyeung/github/paper2notes/dse-classified/mc/05_Radioactivity_and_Nuclear_Energy/25_Radiation_and_Radioactivity/` and matching `lq/` folder
- Question bank: `/Users/sinchunyeung/github/paper2notes/QB_501/` (`5_ch01_MC_e.pdf`, `5_ch01_SQ_e.pdf`, `5_ch01_LQ_e.pdf`, and answer PDFs)

Tools available: `pdftoppm`, `pdfimages`, `pdfinfo`, `tesseract`.

### Required deliverables (write only inside the worktree)
1. `notes/_source/book5-ch01/ocr.md` - OCR transcript of Book 5 Chapter 1 only (not the whole book). Preserve section headings and figure captions; mark unclear OCR with `[?]`. Include a short front-matter block: page range used, how chapter boundaries were identified.
2. `notes/_source/book5-ch01/images/` - extracted figures/diagrams useful for later notes (prefer clean diagram crops over full-page dumps). Add `notes/_source/book5-ch01/images/INDEX.md` listing each file, source page, caption/topic, and suggested use in notes (static vs animate later).
3. `notes/_source/book5-ch01/problems.md` - problem shortlist for this chapter from HKDSE MC/LQ section 25 and QB_501, ordered to match textbook section flow. For each item: id/source, topic tag, why it fits, and whether it is a concept-check candidate vs worked example. Prefer quality over dumping every question.
4. `notes/_source/book5-ch01/outline.md` - chapter concept outline in textbook order, noting which ideas should become visuals/animations vs short text, and where concept checks belong.
5. `.cursor/rules/visual-html-notes.mdc` - always-available rule with `globs: notes/**` (and `alwaysApply: false`) describing project needs: visual-first HTML notes, minimize prose, prefer interactive/non-interactive diagrams and animations, follow Active Physics textbook order, use `_source` materials, add concept checks, keep HKDSE/QB examples sparse and purposeful. Keep the rule concise and actionable (< ~80 lines). Create this rule only after the source consumption artifacts above exist.

### Process order
OCR/outline/images/problems first; Cursor rule last; then commit all of it.

### Constraints
- Do not commit `active-physics/`, `QB_501/`, or `dse-classified/` (gitignored).
- Do not invent physics content that is not supported by the sources; flag gaps in the outline.
- Do not build the full HTML notes chapter in this task.
- One or two clear commits on the task branch is enough.

## Captain's intent
Build the first draft HTML notes for Active Physics Book 5 Chapter 1 (syllabus Ch.25 Radiation and Radioactivity).

Favour visuals over text: static diagrams, animations, and interactive controls. Be example-driven. For instance, teach how to distinguish alpha, beta, and gamma by drawing the identification procedure as a directed graph (decision flow), not a wall of prose. Prefer showing the procedure (absorbers, electric/magnetic deflection, cloud-chamber tracks) as interactive or animated diagrams with minimal labels.

Use the existing intake under `notes/_source/book5-ch01/` (outline, OCR, problem shortlist, figure crops) and the Cursor rule for `notes/**`. Do not invent physics beyond those sources; flag gaps.

## Firstmate spec
Mode is no-mistakes (product-facing notes). Implement, commit, then run the project's no-mistakes pipeline through a green PR.

### Bring intake onto this branch first
`main` does not yet contain the source intake. After creating `fm/p2n-b5ch1-notes-book-5-ch1-first-draft-visual-html-notes-87`, incorporate the ready intake branch before writing notes:

```sh
git merge --ff-only fm/p2n-b5ch1-book-5-ch1-radiation-notes-intake-ocr-im-0b
```

If ff-only fails, cherry-pick in order: `6c54619` then `083a624` (titles: source intake, then visual-html-notes rule). Do not rewrite intake history. Confirm `notes/_source/book5-ch01/{ocr,outline,problems}.md`, `images/`, and `.cursor/rules/visual-html-notes.mdc` are present.

### Notes deliverable
Create a first-draft chapter under `notes/` that a student can open in a browser with no build step (plain HTML/CSS/JS; relative assets OK).

Suggested layout (adjust only if clearer):
- `notes/book5/ch01-radiation-and-radioactivity/index.html` - chapter shell / nav in textbook order
- Section pages or single-page sections matching `outline.md` (25.1 → 25.2 → …)
- Colocated CSS/JS next to the HTML; keep dependencies local (no CDN requirement)
- Optional: `notes/book5/ch01-radiation-and-radioactivity/assets/` for SVG/CSS-drawn figures (prefer redrawn SVG/CSS/canvas over embedding `_source` PNG crops as final art; crops are redraw references)

### Visual / pedagogy bar (must meet)
1. **Visuals first:** each idea opens with a diagram, animation, or interactive control; prose is labels, one-liners, and equations only.
2. **Example-driven:** teach via concrete procedures and worked visuals. Include at least one **directed-graph / flowchart** interaction for distinguishing α, β, γ (nodes = observations or tests such as paper / Al / Pb, deflection in E or B, track shape; edges = yes/no or outcome; user can step or click through).
3. **Animate processes** where the outline calls for them (ionization knockout, X-ray tube, decay equations, ion pairs, GM pulses, E/B deflection, absorber stacks).
4. **Concept checks** after each major idea, preferring items tagged `concept-check` in `problems.md` (interactive T/F, pick-diagram, or short calc). At most one worked example per section.
5. Follow textbook order from `outline.md`. Respect recorded gaps (PDF missing printed pp.1–3; do not invent opener content).
6. If the Cursor rule needs a one-line addition for "example-driven directed graphs / decision flows", update `.cursor/rules/visual-html-notes.mdc` in the same change set.

### Out of scope
- Do not commit `active-physics/`, `QB_501/`, or `dse-classified/`
- Do not build later chapters
- Polish pass can follow; this is a coherent first draft students can click through, not a sparse stub

### Done
Pipeline green PR; report the full https PR URL on the ready status line.

## Captain's intent
Create a blog-style HTML artifact that explains how the current Simplification of Trajectory Streams algorithm works, and how DOTS, SQUISH, and Douglas-Peucker (DP) work, with mathematical notation, visualizations, proof-of-correctness notes where the sources support them, and a references section.

## Firstmate spec
Mode is local-only. Commit only tracked changes that belong in git (at minimum the `.gitignore` update for `draft/`). The HTML under `draft/` must remain untracked because it is gitignored.

### Deliverable
- `draft/trajectory-stream-simplification-explainer.html` (single self-contained file preferred; colocated CSS/JS/SVG assets under `draft/` are OK if also ignored by the same `draft/` rule)
- Update `.gitignore` with a clear `draft/` entry (and a one-line comment that draft blog/explainer artifacts are local-only)

### Content requirements (ground in THIS repo)
Read and cite the project's own sources before writing:
- `README.md`, `simplify.cpp`, `simplify_geometry.h`, related headers
- `papers/` (`journal.pdf`, `dots.pdf`, `squish.pdf`, `benchmark.pdf`) and arXiv link already in README: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.23025
